column1: # The independent oracle for the Phase-7 evidence calculus: a hand-authored claim
# inventory for one existing phase.
# The phase is Phase 5, the lift calculus. It is chosen because it is finished, small
# enough to inventory by hand, and discharges its claims by three different instruments —
# two authored tables, a scan of the source the compiler sees, and two compile-fail pairs
# — so the inventory exercises more than one fixture kind.
# Authored from `documents/engineering/evidence_calculus_doctrine.md` sections 2, 3 and 5,
# read against `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN/phase_05_lift_calculus.md`. Every row below is read off
# the *contract*, never off the registry the implementation derives, which is what lets
# this table stay red when the derivation is wrong.
# Four rules decide the rows:
#   one fixture   every claim names exactly one, because a claim discharged by "the suite"
#                 is discharged by nothing in particular and stays green when the one
#                 relevant case is deleted
#   strength      a claim may say only what its fixture's kind entitles it to. A
#                 compile-fail fixture entitles a claim to `this-expression-rejected` and
#                 to nothing stronger; an authored table entitles it to
#                 `satisfies-authored-predicate`
#   register      Phase 5 is a Register-1 contract, so every fixture here runs `pure`.
#                 A row claiming otherwise would be declaring a register its fixture
#                 cannot reach, which section 5 calls its own illegal state
#   mutant        a claim held by a mutation argument names the mutant and the locus that
#                 mutant must redden. Its fixture is the one registry, because that is
#                 where the expectation — the locus — is actually authored
# The two rows whose fixture is `test/mutant/registry.tsv` are the self-referential case
# section 4 names: no expectation for them can be authored outside the machinery, so what
# stands in for independence is that a named check reddens when a named defect is seeded.
# claim<TAB>fixture_kind<TAB>fixture<TAB>strength<TAB>register<TAB>mutant<TAB>locus
the layer set is closed at three members
the transition relation admits exactly the pairs the doctrine admits
no dispatch over the layer set carries a catch-all arm
a witness exists only where an observation reported the transition's precondition
a runtime-assembled plan joins two transitions only when they meet
a witness cannot be written down
two paths whose layers do not meet cannot be composed
